name: the Cyclopean Monolith
summary: A vast, ancient stone monolith rising from an abyss at the bottom of the sea, carved with aquatic hieroglyphics and worshipped by a fish-like creature that emerged from the water to embrace it.
description:
Rising about a hundred yards across the valley, the Cyclopean Monolith first appeared to the narrator as a vast and singular object gleaming whitely in the light of the ascendant moon. Closer inspection showed it to be a gigantic, well-shaped piece of stone whose contour and position seemed not altogether the work of Nature, but rather the workmanship — and perhaps the worship — of living and thinking creatures. It stood within an abyss that had yawned at the bottom of the sea since the world was young.

The monolith's surface bore inscriptions and crude sculptures in a system of hieroglyphics unknown to the narrator, consisting for the most part of conventionalized aquatic symbols such as fishes, eels, octopi, crustaceans, molluscs, and whales. Some of the bas-reliefs depicted fish-like men disporting themselves in water, or paying homage at a monolithic shrine that appeared to be under the waves as well.

A vast, scaly creature rose from the water and flung its gigantic arms about the monolith, bowing its hideous head and giving vent to certain measured sounds, as if performing some rite of worship before the ancient stone.

Across the chasm, the wavelets washed the base of the Cyclopean monolith; on whose surface I could now trace both inscriptions and crude sculptures.
